details.label: Discussion
details.text: The northern extension of an MCS has sustained a bowing structure over northern IL with an eastward system motion of around 40 kt. An outflow boundary associated with an area of thunderstorms farther east extends from the vicinity of the bow echo south-southeast through eastern IL into southwest IN. The presence of that boundary may result in the MCS turning more to the southeast over the next hour to two, fueled by a strongly unstable environment, per the 12Z DVN sounding. The current DVN VWP is sampling 35-50 kt west-northwesterly winds in the 1-6 km layer, which are oriented largely perpendicular to the bow, likely maintaining a robust rear-inflow jet. As such, damaging winds are expected to continue with gusts up to 75 mph possible as the system advances toward northwest and west-central IN. Extrapolation of the current motion takes it to the eastern edge of the watch by 1530Z, likely requiring an additional watch
